question: Under Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-7, which baseline requirement must every applicant for a Mississippi resident real estate broker's license satisfy, regardless of which experience path (12-month, 36-month, or the alternative education track) they use to qualify?
choice_a: Be at least eighteen (18) years of age and maintain a licensed brokerage office physically located in Mississippi
choice_b: Be at least twenty-one (21) years of age and have legal domicile in the State of Mississippi at the time of application
choice_c: Be a United States citizen who has resided in Mississippi continuously for at least five (5) years
choice_d: Hold a four-year bachelor's degree and be at least twenty-five (25) years of age
explanation: Section 73-35-7 requires every applicant for a resident broker's license to be age 21 or over and have legal domicile in Mississippi at the time of application, and also to be subject to the state's jurisdiction, income tax, and road/bridge privilege tax laws, and not be an elector in any other state. This baseline age-and-domicile requirement applies no matter which of the statute's alternative experience or education tracks the applicant otherwise uses to qualify.

question: Under the standard broker qualification track (not the alternative education path), how long must an applicant have held an active Mississippi real estate salesperson's license immediately prior to applying to sit for the broker's examination?
choice_a: Six (6) months
choice_c: Twelve (12) months
choice_d: Twenty-four (24) months
explanation: Section 73-35-7(d) requires an applicant on the standard track to have held a license as an active real estate salesperson for twelve (12) months prior to making application for the broker's examination, in addition to completing the required coursework, passing the exam, and clearing the background investigation. This 12-month track is the one that carries the statute's separate hiring-restriction affidavit requirement, unlike the alternative 36-month experience track.

question: A broker applicant chooses to wait until she has held an active salesperson's license for thirty-six (36) months (rather than the minimum twelve) before applying for the broker's examination. What specific benefit does taking this longer path give her under §73-35-7?
choice_a: Complete exemption from the broker's licensing examination
choice_b: A reduced broker application fee compared to the 12-month track
choice_c: Automatic waiver of the required real estate coursework hours
choice_d: She is not required to sign the affidavit restricting the hiring of salespersons for thirty-six (36) months after licensure
explanation: Applicants who qualify on the standard 12-month track must sign a perjury-form affidavit stating they will not hire any real estate salespersons for 36 months from the date their own active salesperson's license was approved. Section 73-35-7 provides that this hiring restriction does not apply to an applicant who instead held an active salesperson's license for at least 36 months prior to applying for the broker's examination — that applicant may hire salespersons immediately upon becoming a broker.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-7, paragraph (h) and the immediately following paragraph on the 36-month track

question: A newly licensed broker who qualified under the standard 12-month salesperson-experience track is required to sign a form under penalty of perjury when applying. What does that affidavit certify under §73-35-7?
choice_a: That the broker will not hire any real estate salespersons for thirty-six (36) months from the date his or her own active salesperson's license was approved
choice_b: That the broker will complete 120 classroom hours of coursework within one year of licensure
choice_c: That the broker will maintain errors and omissions insurance coverage for the following renewal biennium
choice_d: That the broker will not open a branch office within 36 months of licensure
explanation: Section 73-35-7(h) requires an applicant using the 12-month experience track to sign, under penalty of perjury, a Commission-created standard form stating the applicant will not hire any real estate salespersons for 36 months from the date of approval of his or her own active real estate salesperson's license. Once that 36-month restriction period lapses, the broker is authorized to employ any number of real estate salespersons.

question: In addition to examination and background-clearance requirements, how many hours of real estate coursework must a broker applicant on the standard experience track successfully complete under §73-35-7?
choice_a: Sixty (60) hours
choice_c: Ninety (90) hours
choice_d: Forty-five (45) hours
explanation: Section 73-35-7(e) requires a broker applicant to have successfully completed a minimum of one hundred twenty (120) hours of real estate courses. This is double the sixty (60) hours the same statute requires of a resident salesperson applicant, reflecting the higher educational standard set for broker licensure.

question: An applicant who has NOT held an active real estate salesperson's license for at least thirty-six (36) months prior to submitting an application may still qualify for a broker's license by completing what alternative educational requirement under §73-35-7?
choice_a: Ninety (90) hours of Commission-sponsored seminars in any subject
choice_b: Any bachelor's degree in an unrelated field plus two years of unlicensed brokerage employment
choice_c: One hundred fifty (150) classroom hours in real estate courses that are acceptable for credit toward a degree at a college or university approved by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools (or comparable regional accreditor)
choice_d: Sixteen (16) hours of continuing education plus a personal letter of recommendation from a licensed broker
explanation: Section 73-35-7 provides that an applicant who has not held an active real estate salesperson's license for at least 36 months prior to submitting an application must have successfully completed a minimum of 150 classroom hours in real estate courses that are acceptable for credit toward a degree at a SACS-accredited (or comparable regional accreditor) college or university. This is the statute's degree-program alternative to the salesperson-experience requirement.

question: Per MREC Rule 1.1, what minimum passing scores must a Mississippi broker applicant achieve on the National Portion and the State-Specific Portion of the broker's licensing examination, respectively?
choice_a: 70% National / 75% State-Specific
choice_c: 80% National / 85% State-Specific
choice_d: 75% National / 80% State-Specific
explanation: Rule 1.1(A) requires a broker applicant to pass the National Portion with a grade of at least 75% and the State-Specific Portion with a grade of at least 80%. By comparison, Rule 1.1(B) sets the salesperson's examination thresholds lower, at 70% National and 75% State-Specific, consistent with the statute's more exacting standard for broker licensure.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Chapter 1, Rule 1.1(A)

question: Once an applicant is approved to test, MREC Rule 1.1(E) gives the applicant how long to take and pass both the National and State-Specific portions of the examination before the application fee is forfeited and the file is closed?
choice_a: Two (2) months
choice_c: Six (6) months
choice_d: One (1) year
explanation: Rule 1.1(E) states that once an applicant is approved, the applicant has two months in which to take and pass both the National Portion and the State-Specific Portion of the examination. If the applicant fails to appear within that two-month window, the fee is forfeited and the file is closed.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Chapter 1, Rule 1.1(E)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-13, an applicant who fails the Mississippi broker's examination on two occasions must wait how long before becoming eligible to take the examination again?
choice_a: Three (3) months
choice_c: One (1) year
choice_d: Ninety (90) days
explanation: Section 73-35-13(3) provides that an individual who fails the broker's examination on two occasions is ineligible for a similar examination until six months have passed from the last attempt, and then only upon making a new application. This is twice the three-month waiting period the same subsection sets for a salesperson applicant who fails twice.

question: Since July 1, 2016, applicants for a Mississippi broker's license, a resident salesperson's license, or a nonresident's license — and all license renewal applicants — must comply with which requirement under §73-35-10?
choice_a: A civil-litigation history disclosure notarized by a Mississippi attorney
choice_b: A personal credit report submitted directly to the Commission by a licensed credit bureau
choice_c: A fingerprint-based criminal history records check of the Mississippi central criminal database and the FBI criminal history database
choice_d: Proof of continuous Mississippi residency for the preceding five years
explanation: Section 73-35-10(1)(b) requires that, from and after July 1, 2016, all applicants for a Mississippi broker's license, resident salesperson's license, or nonresident's license, and all license renewal applicants, undergo a fingerprint-based criminal history records check of the Mississippi central criminal database and the FBI criminal history database as part of the Commission's background investigation.

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-17(4), on what license renewal cycle may the Mississippi Real Estate Commission require licensees to register and pay their renewal fee?
choice_a: Only annually, with no exceptions permitted
choice_c: Only biennially, with no annual option ever available
choice_d: Annually or biennially, at the Commission's discretion
explanation: Section 73-35-17(4) directs licensees to register annually or biennially, in the discretion of the Commission, according to rules the Commission promulgates. In current practice the Commission has set a two-year (biennial) renewal cycle for individual licenses, matching MREC Rule 2.1's two-year renewal fee schedule, but the statute itself authorizes either cycle length.

question: If a Mississippi licensee fails to pay a renewal fee when due, §73-35-17(4) provides for automatic cancellation of the license after how much written notice of delinquency, and what penalty applies to a licensee who renews within that grace period?
choice_a: Two (2) months' written notice; a one hundred percent (100%) penalty of the renewal fee
choice_b: One (1) month's notice; a fifty percent (50%) penalty
choice_c: Thirty (30) days' notice; a twenty-five percent (25%) penalty
choice_d: Six (6) months' notice; a fifty percent (50%) penalty
explanation: Section 73-35-17(4) states that a licensee failing to pay the renewal fee, after two months' written notice of delinquency delivered by email to the licensee (and the responsible broker, if applicable), will have the license automatically cancelled. Any licensee who renews within that two-month grace period must pay a penalty equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the renewal fee — a fact also reflected in MREC Rule 2.1's fee schedule.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-17(4); see also MREC Rule 2.1(C)

question: How many clock hours of Commission-approved continuing education coursework must each individual licensee complete per two-year license renewal cycle under §73-35-18(1)?
choice_a: Twelve (12) hours
choice_c: Twenty (20) hours
choice_d: Eight (8) hours
explanation: Section 73-35-18(1) requires each individual license renewal applicant to submit proof of completion of not less than sixteen (16) clock hours of approved course work, and this requirement applies to each two-year license renewal cycle.

question: Of the sixteen (16) required continuing education clock hours per renewal cycle, §73-35-18(1) caps the number of hours the Commission may designate as mandatory required subject matter at what maximum?
choice_a: Four (4) hours
choice_c: Eight (8) hours
choice_d: All sixteen (16) hours may be mandated
explanation: Section 73-35-18(1) permits the Commission to determine required subject matter within the mandated sixteen hours, but expressly limits that required subject matter to no more than eight (8) of the total sixteen (16) hours, leaving the remaining hours to be satisfied with elective approved coursework.

question: A licensee earns twenty-two (22) approved continuing education hours during the final three (3) months of her renewal cycle. Under §73-35-18(1), at most how many of those excess hours (beyond the required 16) may be carried over and credited toward the next renewal period?
choice_a: All excess hours, with no cap on carryover
choice_c: Ten (10) hours
choice_d: Six (6) hours
explanation: Section 73-35-18(1) provides that approved continuing education hours earned in the final three months of a licensee's renewal period, if in excess of the required minimum sixteen hours, may be carried over and credited to the next renewal period, but no more than six (6) hours may be carried over in this manner — regardless of how many excess hours were actually earned.

question: Under §73-35-18(2), a licensee applying for the FIRST renewal of a newly issued license is exempt from the continuing education requirement if the license has been held for no more than what period?
choice_a: One (1) year
choice_c: Two (2) years
choice_d: Eighteen (18) months
explanation: Section 73-35-18(2) provides that an applicant for first renewal who has been licensed for not more than one (1) year is not required to comply with the continuing education requirement for that first renewal, recognizing that a brand-new licensee has not yet had a full cycle to accumulate CE hours.

question: Section 73-35-18(2) grants a complete, ongoing continuing-education exemption to licensees who meet which combined threshold?
choice_a: Held a license for at least ten (10) years AND are older than sixty (60) years of age
choice_b: Held a Mississippi broker's or salesperson's license for at least twenty-five (25) years AND are older than sixty-five (65) years of age
choice_c: Are on inactive status for any length of time, regardless of years licensed
choice_d: Currently serve as a member of the Mississippi Real Estate Commission
explanation: Section 73-35-18(2) states that the continuing education provisions do not apply to persons who have held a broker's or salesperson's license in Mississippi for at least twenty-five (25) years and who are older than sixty-five (65) years of age — both conditions must be met for this exemption to apply.

question: An inactive Mississippi licensee wants to reactivate her license. Under §73-35-18(2), what must she do regarding continuing education before the Commission will restore active status?
choice_a: Nothing — inactive licensees are permanently exempt from all future CE obligations once reactivated
choice_b: Retake the entire pre-license course regardless of how many CE hours were missed
choice_c: Cumulatively satisfy the continuing education requirements missed during the period the license was inactive
choice_d: Pay a flat $50 continuing-education waiver fee in lieu of completing any hours
explanation: Section 73-35-18(2) provides that inactive licensees are not required to meet the CE requirements while inactive; however, before activating the license to active status, the licensee must cumulatively meet the continuing education requirements missed during the period the license was inactive. A related exception allows a licensee at least 30 hours in arrears to instead retake pre-license coursework in full, at the Commission's discretion.

question: Per MREC Rule 2.1, what is the maximum fee for a broker's license application (including one year's use of the license), and what is the maximum fee to renew an individual broker's license for a full two-year period?
choice_a: $75 application / $100 two-year renewal
choice_c: $150 application / $200 two-year renewal
choice_d: $100 application / $150 two-year renewal
explanation: Rule 2.1(A)(1) sets the broker application fee (including one year's use of the license) at $100, and Rule 2.1(C)(1) sets the maximum two-year renewal fee for an individual broker at $150 — figures consistent with the underlying statutory caps in Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-17 ($100 application; $75/year renewal cap, i.e., $150 for two years).

question: A Mississippi broker licensed in another state wants to obtain a Mississippi license without retaking the Mississippi examination. Under Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-13(6), when is the Commission authorized to grant this examination exemption by reciprocity?
choice_a: When the Commission determines the examination administered in the applicant's home state is equivalent to Mississippi's exam, and that state extends the same reciprocal exemption privilege to Mississippi licensees
choice_b: Automatically, for any applicant who has held an out-of-state broker's license for at least one year
choice_c: Only if the applicant is a Mississippi resident who has never held a license in any other state
choice_d: Only if the applicant pays double the standard application fee in lieu of testing
explanation: Section 73-35-13(6) authorizes the Commission to exempt from examination, in whole or in part, a real estate licensee of another state who desires a Mississippi license, but only if the examination administered in that other state is determined by the Commission to be equivalent to the Mississippi examination, and only if that other state extends this same reciprocal privilege or exemption to Mississippi real estate licensees. Reciprocity for military-trained applicants and military spouses is separately governed by Miss. Code Ann. §73-50-1 or §73-50-2.
